## Structure and components

- [statement] Atlas’s overall fixture contains question, ground_truth and generated answer, omitting contexts. Its answer_similarity output compares answer meaning with the reference; answer_correctness additionally measures factual agreement with that reference. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures · also: https://docs.ragas.io/en/v0.1.21/concepts/metrics/semantic_similarity.html, https://docs.ragas.io/en/v0.1.21/concepts/metrics/answer_correctness.html
- [statement] RAGAS v0.1.21 defines answer_correctness as a weighted combination of semantic similarity and factual overlap. Its factual component classifies statements into shared facts, answer-only facts and omitted reference facts, then computes an F1 score. (medium confidence) — https://docs.ragas.io/en/v0.1.21/concepts/metrics/answer_correctness.html · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures · also: https://docs.ragas.io/en/v0.1.21/concepts/metrics/semantic_similarity.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The inspected Atlas fixture maps question to QUESTIONS and correct_answer to GROUND_TRUTH. Its source context supplies corpus text; evaluator contexts instead contains retrieved doc.page_content lists. The retrieval Dataset contains question, ground_truth and contexts, without a generated answer. Its ground_truth is a reference-answer string, rather than a list of relevant document identifiers. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures
- [statement] Atlas inspects per-question output through result.to_pandas() and answer_correctness < 0.7. It warns that wrong references and sentence-versus-short-answer differences can depress scores. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas’s completion-model fixture adds generated answer to question, ground_truth and retrieved contexts, but selects faithfulness and answer_relevancy. Google’s implementation corroborates that these two named metrics do not require ground-truth answers. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures · also: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/llamaindex-for-rag-on-google-cloud?hl=en
- [statement] Atlas’s completion loop generates an answer through the chain, then separately invokes the retriever to populate evaluation contexts. Consequently, the code does not capture the exact generation-time retrieval result as its evaluation artifact. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures
- [statement] Atlas passes that three-field fixture to context_precision. Ragas v0.1.21 judges each retrieved chunk against the question and reference answer, then rewards relevant chunks appearing earlier in the returned order. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures · also: https://docs.ragas.io/en/v0.1.21/concepts/metrics/context_precision.html
- [statement] Atlas context_recall uses the same reference-answer fixture. Ragas v0.1.21 defines its score as the fraction of ground-truth statements attributable to retrieved context, so this output measures reference-statement coverage. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures · also: https://docs.ragas.io/en/v0.1.21/concepts/metrics/context_recall.html
- [statement] Fixture names require explicit mapping: Atlas stores generated text as answer and its reference as ground_truth; the independent Hugging Face cookbook stores generated_answer and true_answer, then judges against the latter using a 1–5 rubric. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/ai-integrations/langchain/evaluate-rag.md · keywords: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures · also: https://huggingface.co/learn/cookbook/rag_evaluation
